Feature: Independent control register for each GPIO.
Test Description: Validate default reset values and masked read/write behavior for GPIO_8 to GPIO_27 control registers via register interface. Only readable fields are compared; only writable fields are updated. A known dynamic input bit is ignored during default comparison.
Meta Test Description:
The test performs two phases:
1) Default value check (chk_rst_val): For each address in addr_array, skip entries flagged in skip_rst_array or those with read_mask==0. Read the register, mask out bit0 (0xFFFFFFFE) to ignore a dynamic DIN-related bit, and compare against the corresponding expected default in default_value_array. Increment def_fail_cnt on mismatch.

For each address not skipped and with nonzero write_mask, write (pattern & write_mask). Then, for each such address that is both writable and readable (read_mask!=0), read back (read_reg(addr) & read_mask). Compute wr_n = (~write_mask), then the expected value exp_val = ((pattern & read_mask & write_mask) | (wr_n & read_mask & default_value)). Compare data_rd with exp_val and increment wr_fail_cnt on mismatch. Test ends with finish(0) if both def_fail_cnt and wr_fail_cnt are zero; otherwise finish(1). A soft-reset routine exists but is compiled out (#ifdef 0).

title: GPIO Negative-Edge Interrupt Enable and Service Validation
objective: Ensure each GPIO pin generates a negative-edge interrupt when driven from high to low, that masked status sets and clears correctly, and that the system interrupt controller latches and clears the interrupt.
steps: Enable the GPIO instance interrupt in the system interrupt controller (intr_en1) and enable the corresponding GIC IRQ.
Drive all GPIO inputs high via the external stimulus register at 0xA0243FFC.
Configure each per-GPIO control register (gpio_8 to gpio_39) for negative-edge detection and enable its interrupt.
For each pin: clear any existing raw interrupt, enable its masked interrupt (intr1_intr_en1), then generate a falling edge only on that pin using 0xA0243FFC.
Wait for the ISR to run and service the interrupt; flag a failure if it times out.

In the ISR: verify the pin’s masked status is set (intr1_intr_sts1), ensure the input/flag reflects the falling edge, clear the raw interrupt (gpio_intr_raw_stclr1), confirm masked status clears, and clear the system raw status (raw_stcr1) and GIC IRQ.
Repeat for all pins and report the overall result.
expected_result: All pins generate and service a negative-edge interrupt within the timeout; masked status sets for the targeted pin and clears after raw clear; system raw status is cleared and the GIC is acknowledged; no errors are reported.

Feature: interrupts can be generated based on positive edge or negative edge or level high or level low detection at GPIO input.
Test Description: Validate positive-edge interrupt generation when enabling interrupts on all GPIO pads. The test configures each per-GPIO control register for positive-edge detection, sets GPIOs to input mode, enables the group interrupt, generates a rising edge on inputs, and verifies the group masked status asserts and clears. It also clears the system-level pending status and re-enables interrupts for subsequent iterations.
Meta Test Description:
test_case():
- If GPIO0 build: GIC_EnableIRQ(87). If GPIO1 build: GIC_EnableIRQ(88).
- test_err = 0.
- If GPIO0: write_reg(intr_en1, LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO0_INTR). If GPIO1: write_reg(intr_en1, LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO1_INTR).
- For i = 0..31: write_reg(gp0_gpio_8 + (i*4), 0x00020000) to enable positive-edge interrupt per pin (bit17=1).
- wait_on(10).
- Configure input mode across pads: write_reg(gpio_io_ctrl_group1, 0x000000FF); write_reg(gpio_io_ctrl_group2, 0x000000FF); write_reg(gpio_io_ctrl_group3, 0x000000FF); write_reg(gpio_io_ctrl_group4, 0x000000FF).
- wait_on(10).
- Enable masked interrupts for the group: write_reg(gp0_intr2_intr_en1, 0xFFFFFFFF).
- For i = 0..31 loop:
  - Drive external stimulus low then high to produce a single rising edge: write_reg(0xA0243FFC, 0x00000000); wait_on(10); set int_pend = 1; write_reg(0xA0243FFC, 0xFFFFFFFF).
  - Timeout wait: timeout = 2000; while (int_pend == 1 && --timeout > 0) wait_on(10).
  - If timeout == 0: printf("ERROR: Timeout waiting for GPIO IRQ at i=%u", i); test_err++; break.
  - Optionally drive low again for next iteration: write_reg(0xA0243FFC, 0x00000000); wait_on(10).
- finish(test_err).

Default_IRQHandler():
- wr_val = (1 << i); int_pend = 0.
- rdata_grp = read_reg(gp0_intr1_intr_sts1); mask group during service: write_reg(gp0_intr2_intr_en1, 0x00000000).
- If (rdata_grp & 0xFFFFFFFF) != 0: success log (if enabled) else: print error and increment test_err.
- Clear per-pin raw status for all 32 pins: for j = 0..31: write_reg(gp0_gpio_8 + (j*4), 0x00010000). wait_on(2).
- Read group status again: rdata_grp = read_reg(gp0_intr1_intr_sts1). If rdata_grp == 0x0: success; else: print error and test_err++.
- If GPIO0: write_reg(raw_stcr1, LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO0_INTR); rdata = read_reg(raw_stcr1); if (rdata & LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO0_INTR) != 0 then error++.
- If GPIO1: write_reg(raw_stcr1, LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO1_INTR); rdata = read_reg(raw_stcr1); if (rdata & LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO1_INTR) != 0 then error++.
- Re-enable group masked interrupts: write_reg(gp0_intr2_intr_en1, 0xFFFFFFFF).
- If GPIO0: GIC_ClearIRQ(87); If GPIO1: GIC_ClearIRQ(88).
Remarks: Ensure the corresponding GPIO instance interrupt is enabled in the system interrupt controller before testing and that the external stimulus at 0xA0243FFC is routed to GPIO inputs. Mask the group interrupt during ISR service to avoid re-entrancy, clear all per-pin raw statuses, verify the group status returns to zero, and clear the system-level raw status before re-enabling interrupts.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1) Enable the GPIO instance interrupt in the system interrupt controller (intr_en1) and enable the corresponding GIC IRQ line (87 or 88). 2) Configure each per-GPIO control register for positive-edge detection across 32 pins. 3) Set all GPIO pads to input mode using the IO control group registers. 4) Enable the masked group interrupt output. 5) Generate a rising edge on the GPIO inputs and wait for the ISR to run within the timeout. 6) In the ISR, verify that the group masked interrupt status is set, mask the group, clear all per-pin raw statuses, confirm the group status clears, clear the system raw status (raw_stcr1), and then re-enable group interrupts and acknowledge the GIC. 7) Repeat the edge generation and verification loop for the configured iterations and report overall pass/fail.
Meta Test Steps / Procedure:
Initialization: If GPIO0 then GIC_EnableIRQ(87); if GPIO1 then GIC_EnableIRQ(88). test_err = 0. If GPIO0: write_reg(intr_en1, LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO0_INTR). If GPIO1: write_reg(intr_en1, LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO1_INTR). For i=0..31: write_reg(gp0_gpio_8 + i*4, 0x00020000) to enable posedge. wait_on(10). Write 0x000000FF to gpio_io_ctrl_group1..4. wait_on(10). write_reg(gp0_intr2_intr_en1, 0xFFFFFFFF). For i=0..31: write_reg(0xA0243FFC, 0x00000000); wait_on(10); int_pend=1; write_reg(0xA0243FFC, 0xFFFFFFFF); timeout=2000; while(int_pend && --timeout>0) wait_on(10); if(timeout==0){ printf("ERROR: Timeout waiting for GPIO IRQ at i=%u", i); test_err++; break; } write_reg(0xA0243FFC, 0x00000000); wait_on(10). finish(test_err).
ISR: wr_val=(1<<i); int_pend=0; rdata_grp=read_reg(gp0_intr1_intr_sts1); write_reg(gp0_intr2_intr_en1, 0x00000000); if((rdata_grp & 0xFFFFFFFF)==0){ printf("ERROR: Group Interrupt not occured"); test_err++; } for(j=0..31){ write_reg(gp0_gpio_8 + j*4, 0x00010000); } wait_on(2); rdata_grp=read_reg(gp0_intr1_intr_sts1); if(rdata_grp!=0x0){ printf("ERROR : Group Interrupt clear failed: %x", rdata_grp); test_err++; } If GPIO0: write_reg(raw_stcr1, LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO0_INTR); rdata=read_reg(raw_stcr1); if((rdata & LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO0_INTR)!=0){ printf("sysreg status not cleared"); test_err++; } If GPIO1: write_reg(raw_stcr1, LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO1_INTR); rdata=read_reg(raw_stcr1); if((rdata & LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO1_INTR)!=0){ printf("sysreg status not cleared"); test_err++; } write_reg(gp0_intr2_intr_en1, 0xFFFFFFFF); If GPIO0: GIC_ClearIRQ(87); If GPIO1: GIC_ClearIRQ(88).

Validation / Acceptance Criteria: Pass if each generated rising edge triggers the ISR within the timeout, the group masked interrupt status asserts on entry and clears to zero after per-pin raw clear, and the system raw status is cleared in raw_stcr1 before re-enabling interrupts. Any timeout, missing group status set, group status not clearing, or uncleared system raw status results in failure.

title: GPIO Positive-Edge Interrupt Enable on All Pads and Group Status Clear Validation
objective: Ensure enabling positive-edge detection on all GPIO pads produces a group interrupt on rising inputs, that per-pin raw clear operations remove the group status, and that the system interrupt status is cleared.
steps: Enable the GPIO instance interrupt in the system controller and enable the corresponding GIC IRQ (87 or 88).
Configure each GPIO control register for positive-edge detection across all 32 pads.
Set all GPIO pads to input mode using the IO control group registers.
Enable the masked group interrupt output.
Generate a rising edge on the GPIO inputs and wait for the ISR to run within the timeout.

In the ISR, verify that the group masked interrupt status is set, mask the group, clear all per-pin raw statuses, confirm the group status clears, clear the system raw status, re-enable the group interrupt, and acknowledge the GIC.
Repeat the stimulus and validation loop for the required iterations and report the overall result.
expected_result: Each rising edge results in an interrupt serviced within the timeout; the group masked status asserts and clears after raw clear operations; system raw status is cleared before re-enabling interrupts; no errors are reported.
